```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)

# Read the CSV file
df <- readr::read_delim(
  here("data", "df_for_stepwise_regression.csv"),
  delim = ","
)
```

```{r}
# Define the target variable name
target_variable <- "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"

# Define potential predictor variable names, we exclude identifiers, timestamp, and the target itself
potential_predictors <- setdiff(names(df), c("siteid", "TIMESTAMP", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"))

# We keep only numeric predictors 
numeric_predictors <- names(which(sapply(df[, potential_predictors], is.numeric)))
potential_predictors <- numeric_predictors # Use only numeric ones

# Create a subset of the dataframe with only the target and potential predictors
df_subset <- df[, c(target_variable, potential_predictors)]
```

```{r}
# Handle missing values: Remove rows with NA in any selected column
# IMPORTANT: This removes a lot of data if NAs are scattered.
# Alternative: Only remove NAs based on target and predictors actually used in a *specific* model inside the loop,
# but that makes direct AIC comparison tricky as models might be fit on slightly different data subsets.
# Using na.omit() on the relevant subset is usually the standard approach for this type of exercise.
df_clean <- na.omit(df_subset)

# Check dimensions after removing NAs
print(paste("Original dimensions:", dim(df)[1], "rows"))
print(paste("Dimensions after NA removal:", dim(df_clean)[1], "rows"))

# If df_clean is empty or has too few rows, the NA handling might be too aggressive.
if (nrow(df_clean) < (length(potential_predictors) + 2)) {
  stop("Not enough data remaining after removing NAs to perform regression.")
}
```
